record.original_question: Let Omega ⊂⊂ C^n be a smooth pseudoconvex domain. Let Ak (Omegā) = H(Omega) ∩ C k (Omegā) with C k topology, 1 ≤ k ≤ ∞. Is A∞ (Omegā) dense in Ak (Omegā)?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1.1 Let Ω ⊂⊂ Cn be a smooth pseudoconvex domain. Let Ak (Ω̄) = H(Ω) ∩ C k (Ω̄) with C k topology, 1 ≤ k ≤ ∞. Is A∞ (Ω̄) dense in Ak (Ω̄)? -N. Sibony, sibony@anh.matups.fr

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset\subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain (i.e., a relatively compact domain whose boundary $\partial\Omega$ is smooth and which admits a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion function). For each integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le \infty$, let
$$A^k(\overline{\Omega}) = \mathcal{O}(\Omega) \cap C^k(\overline{\Omega}),$$
where $\mathcal{O}(\Omega)$ denotes the space of holomorphic functions on $\Omega$ and $C^k(\overline{\Omega})$ denotes the space of $C^k$ functions up to the boundary, with $A^k(\overline{\Omega})$ equipped with the standard $C^k$ topology (Fréchet topology when $k=\infty$).

Question: Is $A^\infty(\overline{\Omega})$ dense in $A^k(\overline{\Omega})$ for every finite $k \ge 1$?
artifact.category_tag: Several complex variables — approximation on pseudoconvex domains
artifact.status_search_result: The status of this $C^k$-density question for $A^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ inside $A^k(\overline\Omega)$ on general smooth bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$ could not be conclusively determined from the available search results. Related results (e.g., for strictly pseudoconvex, convex, or finite type domains) are known, but a full resolution for arbitrary smooth pseudoconvex domains is not evident.

status_evidence.title: Smooth Pseudoconvex Domains in C^2 (Fornæss–Sibony)
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth pseudoconvex domains in C^2 for which the corona theorem and L^p estimates for ∂̄ fail.
status_evidence.claim: Shows that on general smooth pseudoconvex domains, classical estimates and approximation results can fail, indicating subtlety in $A^k$ questions.
